slug: 2025-12-11 South Sudan to get data protection bill in 2026, says minister

facts.fact: ICT Minister Ateny Wek Ateny said the government will introduce its first-ever Data Protection Bill in 2026, to be drafted jointly by the ministries of information and justice.
The minister announced on 2025-12-11 (article date; event reported as the previous Thursday) that a Data Protection Bill would be introduced in 2026.

facts.fact: Radio Tamazuj reports the country lacks a comprehensive data protection law, and a digital expert at the Excellence Foundation says South Sudan has no data protection laws in place at the moment.

Radio Tamazuj reports that in October 2025 digital security experts finalised drafting the country's first Data Protection Policy Bill, facilitated by Koneta and Paradigm Initiative with the NCA and civil society.
Radio Tamazuj reports that the draft bill, when passed, will establish a Data Protection Commission to safeguard the personal data of South Sudanese online users.

slug: 2025-10-17 Paradigm Initiative partners with Koneta Hub on data protection law in South Sudan

facts.fact: Paradigm Initiative and Koneta Hub held a two-day Juba convening of lawmakers, CSOs and officials to review the draft Data Protection Bill and seek parliamentary commitment to table it; the release is dated 2025-10-17 and gives no separate event date.
Koneta's Executive Director said the country lacks a comprehensive legal and institutional framework for the protection of personal data, with existing ICT regulations limited.
Data Protection Africa's factsheet states South Sudan has no data protection law as of its page-last-updated stamp of 24 May 2022 (the document's published date, used as as_of).

The factsheet says it has been reported that South Sudan has drafted a dedicated data protection bill expected to pass soon; no date is given for the report, so the published date of 24 May 2022 is used.
The factsheet states no data protection authority has been appointed and the country has no law establishing one, as of 24 May 2022 (published date used).
